item: Basis: the lessee's duty to pay the rent at the agreed times (Civil Code, lease chapter, article around 498 as amended by Law 07-05 of 13 May 2007), and the binding force of the contract (article 106).

Is the lease in writing with a certain date? Since Law 07-05 (article 467 bis) a lease must be made in writing with a certain date, on pain of nullity; check the date of the contract against 2007 and how the lease can be proved otherwise.
Element: conclusion of the lease and the agreed rent (amount, periodicity, due dates); attach the lease contract.
Element: the lessee was put in possession / the lease began (date of handing over the premises).
Element: the rent periods left unpaid and the total sum; who must prove payment: the lessor proves the obligation, the lessee proves payment (Civil Code article 323).

Element: formal notice (إعذار) served on the lessee by a bailiff or by registered letter (Civil Code articles 119-120, 180-181), especially before asking rescission or delay damages; check its date and that it preceded the petition.
Exemptions from formal notice: contract clause making the debtor in default on the due date, debtor's written refusal, performance impossible by the debtor's act (article 181).

Rescission: judicial rescission of a synallagmatic contract for non-performance after notice (article 119); the judge may grant a delay; express resolutory clause (article 120) still requires notice unless waived.
Eviction of the lessee as a consequence of rescission; eviction of an occupant without title is a different claim.

Limitation: rent as a periodic renewable right prescribes in five years (Civil Code article 309), counted from each instalment's due date; not raised by the court of its own motion (article 321), only on the debtor's plea.
General limitation of fifteen years (article 308) does not apply to rent arrears; interruption by judicial claim, acknowledgement, or seizure (articles 317-318); suspension (article 316).
How periods are counted: Code of Civil and Administrative Procedure articles 404-405 (full periods, day of the starting act not counted, last day holiday extends).
Competent section: civil section of the tribunal for residential leases; commercial section when the lease is commercial (CPC article 32 and following).
Territorial jurisdiction: for real-property matters and leases, the court where the property is situated (CPC article 40), which is of public order there; otherwise defendant's domicile (article 37).

Commercial leases: Commercial Code articles 169 to 202; after Law 05-02 of 6 February 2005 (article 187 bis) leases concluded after its entry into force end at term without notice to quit or eviction compensation; check which regime applies by contract date.

Commercial lease unpaid rent: rescission/eviction for non-payment of rent is not a refusal of renewal; check that the claim is not actually an expiry/refusal of renewal dispute (notice to quit, article 173).

Administrative courts: if one party is the State, a wilaya, a commune or a public administrative body (CPC article 800-801), the claim may leave the ordinary courts; leases of public domain property are administrative.
Specialised commercial courts (CPC articles 536 bis and following, Law 22-13): unpaid rent between merchants is not usually among their listed matters.
Order to pay (CPC articles 306 and following) as an alternative for a fixed, due debt proved in writing; check whether one was already issued.
Summary proceedings (référé, CPC article 299 and following) for urgent eviction or provisional payment; different from a claim on the merits.
Petition formal elements: CPC articles 14-15 (court, parties' names and domiciles, facts, requests, documents); Arabic language (article 8); standing and interest (article 13).

Land registry publication of petitions about real property rights (CPC article 17 / Decree 76-63 article 85): normally not required for a mere rent claim, but check if rescission of a published lease of more than 12 years is requested.

Accessory requests: delay damages / interest (Civil Code article 182, 186; note interest prohibition between individuals article 454), penalty payment (astreinte, CPC articles 625, 174 Civil Code), costs (CPC article 419), provisional execution (CPC article 323).
Lessor's privilege on movables in the premises (Civil Code article 995) and conservatory seizure (CPC article 646 and following) for rent.
Payment place and set-off: rent payable at the lessee's domicile unless agreed otherwise (article 499); lessee's defences: repairs owed by lessor, deposit (guarantee) offset.
Death of the lessee or transfer of the lease: who is the proper defendant (article 469 bis 1).
Residential leases under Legislative Decree 93-03 on real-estate promotion and Executive Decree 94-69 model contract; public housing (OPGI) leases may involve a public body.
Boundary: claim for occupation indemnity against an occupant without title is not unpaid rent; claim after expiry of commercial lease (eviction compensation) is not unpaid rent.
Boundary: rent of agricultural land is governed by special rules; rent of a public property concession is administrative.
Documents: lease contract, formal notice and bailiff's report, statement of the arrears, proof of ownership or capacity of lessor, receipts.

Amendments to remember: Law 07-05 (2007) on Civil Code lease chapter; Law 05-02 (2005) Commercial Code article 187 bis; Law 22-13 (2022) amending CPC (specialised commercial courts, administrative appeal courts).
Is the plaintiff the lessor (or a person holding the lessor's rights), and is the defendant the lessee named in the lease?
Is there a lease contract, and is its date, term, rent amount and payment dates known?
Is the lease in writing, and does the writing have a certain date (registration) if the lease is over the statutory length?
Is the premises a dwelling, a professional premises or a commercial premises (business asset)?
If commercial: which regime of the Commercial Code governs the lease (before or after the 2005 reform)?
Which rent instalments are unpaid, for which periods, and in what total amount?
Has any rent been paid or any receipt issued, and what does the receipt say?
Was a formal notice (إعذار) served on the lessee to pay, by what means and on what date?
Does the lease set its own form, period or addressee of the notice, and was it respected?
Is the notice a precondition to the claim for rescission or eviction, and what period does it give the lessee?
Does the lease contain a rescission clause (شرط فاسخ) for non-payment, and is it express?
Is the claim only for payment, or also for rescission and eviction?
Which court has subject-matter jurisdiction: the real-property section, the commercial section, or the specialised commercial court?
Which court has territorial jurisdiction: where the premises lie (real property)?
Is the dispute real property so the section for real-property matters hears it?
Is there a section for this matter in the court, or has it been merged?
Is any party a public body so the administrative court could be competent (lease of public property)?
Is the lease of state or public domain property, governed by administrative rules?
Is the property registered at the land registry and does the petition have to be published?
What is the limitation period for rent arrears, and from when does it run?
Has the limitation been interrupted or suspended, and who may raise it?
May the court raise limitation on its own motion?
How is the lease proved, and how is payment proved (receipts, bank transfers)?
Is the rent fixed or has it been revised, and by what agreement?
May the lessee claim set-off or a withholding of rent for defects or repairs?
Are damages for delay, interest or a penalty clause claimed, and on what basis?
Is a payment order (order to pay) procedure available instead of an ordinary claim?
Is the lessee's residence or the premises' address known for service?
Which documents must be attached: lease, receipts, notice, proof of service, extract of land registry?
Is provisional execution requested, and is it justified?
Is the lessee in bankruptcy or abroad, which changes the procedure?
Are there guarantors or co-lessees to be named in the claim?
